title: Shortest Stretch to Reach a Total
statement:
Every day a savings jar receives the amount `deposits[i]` (always positive). You want to reach at least `target` coins using a **stretch of consecutive days**.

Return the **fewest days** in a stretch whose deposits add up to **at least** `target`, or `0` if no stretch is enough.

examples.explanation: The days 4 and 3 add up to 7.
All the deposits together are only 3.

hints.nudge: Because deposits are positive, adding a day only increases the total and removing a day only decreases it.
hints.pattern: Two pointers: grow the right end until you reach the target, then shrink the left end as long as you still do.
hints.pseudocode:
left = 0; sum = 0; best = infinity
for right in 0..n-1:
  sum += deposits[right]
  while sum >= target: best = min(best, right - left + 1); sum -= deposits[left]; left++
return best or 0
hints.walkthrough: Checking every start and end is O(n^2). With positive numbers you can use a sliding window: extend the right end until the sum reaches the target, then record the length and move the left end forward while the sum still reaches the target (each move can only shorten the window). Both pointers only move forward, so O(n) total. If best was never updated return 0.
